chunks: "Sure. I'll start with the idea and then put real transistors in it. An H-bridge is two legs side by side.
Each leg is a high-side switch from the supply down to a middle node, and a low-side switch from that node to ground.
The motor connects between the two middle nodes, which is the crossbar of the H.
If I close the top-left and bottom-right switches, the left node sits at the supply and the right node at ground, so current goes through the motor one way.
Close the top-right and bottom-left and it goes the other way. That's forward and reverse. Now with MOSFETs: low sides are NFETs with the source at ground.
For the high side I'll draw PFETs with the source at the supply, because the gate drive is simplest, and I'll note that a bigger design uses NFETs there with a bootstrap or charge pump.
I draw the body diode on every FET, because when the motor current has to keep flowing after I switch off, those diodes are what catch it.
Then each gate gets its own control line, with a gate driver and dead time so the two FETs in one leg are never on together. I'd also drop a bulk capacitor across the supply."
